rationale: Parent = round 1: end_call_recall 0.967 (29/30), false_end_calls 0, quality 0.885, p50 606 / p90 778. A keep needs recall 30/30 with 0 false ends (epsilon 0), or quality above 0.915, which no round has passed. Rounds 14, 16 and 18 confirm what rounds 13, 15 and 17 found. When the S01/S11 ladder bullet takes recall to 1.0 (round 14), the round still loses on random false ends from labels that flip between runs. S28 ('that's my son's / no credit cards' leading to 'I am sorry to bother you, goodbye') went wrong 2/3 in round 14 and 3/3 in round 16, and the round-1 guard text for exactly this case was in place both times. S36, a disputed label, went wrong in rounds 16 and 18. Round 18 also added an S31 false end and missed S11 twice. Latency is close to the limit: round 16 hit p50 707 and round 18 hit p50 718, both over 700 after adding only about 15-40 words. So more prompt text risks breaking the latency limit as well as the false-end gate. Untried levers don't fit the problem. Gateway adds 40-130ms, which would breach p50. Temperature 0.7 adds sampling noise, the opposite of what's needed, and 0.0 did not stop the flips in rounds 3, 5 and 8. max_completion_tokens 256/512 can't change which action is chosen, only cut off call_summary. A fourth resubmission of the ladder fix would be a coin flip, and a keep would come from noise, not a real improvement. Recommendation to the user, unchanged: (1) re-run the round-1 parent 2-3 times to measure its real false_end_calls rate, which is very likely 1 or more, not 0; (2) resolve the S36 dispute and review S28's run-to-run instability, or allow false_end_calls epsilon=1 at n=30. After that, the round-14 ladder bullet (recall 1.0, p50 627 / p90 763) is the candidate to keep.
